jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: The Inside Job
jokes.joke: Someone broke into my apartment, so I went to a fortune teller to find out who did it. She stared into her crystal ball and said, 'I see the burglar returning tomorrow.' I said, 'To rob me again?' She said, 'No, to give me my half.'

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Unlicensed Psychic
jokes.joke: My house got broken into last week, so I went to a fortune teller. Eighty bucks. She says, 'I see a stranger in your future who will take your belongings.' I said, 'Yeah, he already did, that's why I'm here.' She said, 'Oh, then that'll be a hundred and twenty. Past-life surcharge.'

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Bleacher Nostradamus
jokes.joke: I went to a psychic last week, and she charged me fifty bucks just to tell me my future. I could have gotten the exact same emotional devastation for free sitting in the aluminum bleachers at my kid’s little league game, watching the left fielder eat dandelions while we’re down by fourteen runs.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Crystal Ball Manager
jokes.joke: I went to a fortune teller last week. Turns out she was the most controlling person I've ever met. She didn't just predict my future—she managed it. Crystal ball in one hand, clipboard in the other. “You will meet someone special Thursday… but only if you wear the shirt I already ordered, leave by 6:47, and text me a photo of the outfit for approval.” I walked out with a palm reading and a performance review.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Refund Policy
jokes.joke: I'm embarrassingly trusting. A fortune teller told me, "I see you giving a stranger forty dollars today," and I was like, "Wow, she's amazing." Then I handed her forty dollars. Halfway home I realized that wasn't a prediction, that was an invoice.

scores.comment: Clear setup and conversational delivery, but the past-life surcharge feels arbitrary rather than logically earned. The final turn produces a mild smile, not a strong laugh.

Strong observational comedy with a vivid, recognizable image. The left fielder eating dandelions while the team trails by fourteen runs delivers a concrete, funny payoff. Natural rhythm and economical construction.
The controlling fortune teller is a workable premise, but the extended instructions overexplain it. The performance-review punchline is familiar corporate humor and weaker than the preceding imagery.

Compact, natural first-person delivery with a satisfying reversal. The invoice punchline cleanly exposes the fortune teller's manipulation, although the trick is relatively predictable and limits the surprise.
Clear premise and a clean twist: the psychic is the burglar's accomplice, and the last line carries it. The corrupt-psychic angle is fairly familiar and the turn is somewhat guessable.

Relatable stage image: the dandelion-eating left fielder and being down fourteen runs. 'Free emotional devastation' is a good turn, though the link between the prediction and the bleachers is a little loose.
The clipboard and the 6:47 departure time are fun details. Naming 'controlling' outright flattens the setup, and the 'performance review' button leans on a stock HR template.
Tight and well paced. The self-aware 'trusting' setup is good, and 'that wasn't a prediction, that was an invoice' is a crisp reframe that lands on the final line.
Classic heist twist where the mystic is in on the burglary. Clean setup and punchline, though a familiar narrative angle.
Nice expansion on the fortune teller premise with the past-life surcharge. Stronger comedic rhythm than Joke A.
Relies too much on a descriptive list of micro-details rather than a sharp comedic turn; a bit wordy for the payoff.
Terrific punchline reframing a psychic prediction as an invoice. Excellent use of character naivety and concise delivery.
Clean setup and twist, but the 'my half' payoff is mild and familiar.
Solid escalation with the past-life surcharge; dialogue has good rhythm.
Strong observational pivot with vivid, specific imagery that lands hard.
Tight and well-timed, though the scam-as-prediction shape is recognizable.
Clean misdirection; fortune teller as burglar accomplice lands clearly and ends on the laugh.
Competent structure, but the surcharge turn feels familiar and less sharp than the setup.
Good specific image with the dandelion detail, though it plays more as observation than a strong twist.
Solid escalation from prediction to micromanagement; performance-review tag is effective but somewhat expected.
